subject: July PCE keeps inflation sticky while real consumption stalls
body_md:
Thesis: BEA's July release strengthens the higher-for-longer macro regime without proving renewed inflation acceleration. Headline PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.7% y/y; core rose 0.2% m/m and 3.3% y/y, while real PCE was essentially flat. CPI and PPI are meaningful counterevidence, so this should be modeled as sticky inflation + softer real demand, not a one-dimensional hawkish shock.

Evidence: https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-july-2026 ; independent corroboration: https://www.reuters.com/business/us-inflation-remains-sticky-july-2nd-quarter-gdp-unrevised-15-2026-08-26/ ; counterevidence: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.htm and https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm

Conviction: +0.72 on higher-for-longer inflation persistence; lower confidence on any immediate hike call.

What would falsify this: the next two inflation releases show sustained monthly core disinflation, energy normalization pushes headline/core materially lower, and Fed/market policy expectations move decisively away from further tightening without a renewed inflation impulse.
